pass_summary: Phase 4 lands all 7 tasks with an unusually disciplined signal-safety design: every kill routes through the single `maySignalGroup` gate in `src/runtime/ownership.ts`, the orphan-reap row genuinely requires a live group member that references the worktree, and no code path signals a PID/PGID without ownership proof. The one structural hole is that a FAILED group enumeration is encoded as 'the group is gone' rather than 'unknown', which inverts the module's own refuse-when-unsure rule in the two places it matters most (teardown success reporting, and Guard 5's deletion verdict).

issues.title: A failed group enumeration is indistinguishable from an empty group — teardown reports success and Guard 5 authorises deletion while an orphan may still be running
issues.description:
`realListGroup` (src/runtime/ownership.ts:190-205) returns `[]` on ANY failure — `ps` missing, Bun.spawnSync throwing, ps exiting non-zero, unparsable output — and `listGroupMembers` (:230) additionally wraps the call in `safe(..., [])`. There is no `null`/unknown state. Three consequences, all in the unsafe direction:

1. `maySignalGroup` (:299-300) maps an empty list to `{kind:"gone"}`, and `stopOwnedGroup` (src/runtime/teardown.ts:265-279) treats `gone` as SUCCESS: it returns `ok:true`, reports "process group N has no live members — the runtime is already stopped", and **removes the pidfile**. If enumeration merely failed, Sentinal has just destroyed the only ownership record for a group that is still running — the exact failure the module's own docstring (ownership.ts:210-219) says must never happen ("Answering 'success' to the second leaves an orphan running while reporting it cleaned up").
2. `ownsLiveRuntime`'s `stale` branch (src/runtime/pidfile.ts:354-359) does `members.length === 0 -> {live:false}`, so the same probe failure makes Guard 5 return "nothing running" and **authorise a directory deletion**. This is precisely the asymmetry the function's docstring (:303-317) claims to implement ("anything it cannot rule out counts as live") — the asymmetry holds for `unreadable`/`foreign`/`owned` but NOT for `stale` + unenumerable group.
3. `preflight`'s stale/orphan row (src/runtime/preflight.ts:281-291) then sees `r.ok === true`, re-probes the port, and if the orphan happens to have released the port (or the contract has no http probe) proceeds to `kind:"spawn"` on top of it.

This contrasts directly with the deliberate opposite choice made for liveness: `probeAlive` (pidfile.ts:233-240) and `safeAlive` (teardown.ts:332-348) both default to ALIVE on probe failure, with explicit comments explaining why. `listGroup` should follow the same rule and does not.

A regression would NOT go red: `src/runtime/ownership.test.ts:263-271` ("is empty when the group cannot be enumerated at all") asserts the current behaviour as intended, so the hole is locked in by test.
issues.suggested_fix: Make enumeration failure a distinct state. In `src/runtime/ownership.ts`, have `realListGroup` return `number[] | null` (null when `Bun.spawnSync` throws or `ps` exits non-zero — check `r.exitCode`), widen `GroupProbes.listGroup` to `number[] | null`, and have `listGroupMembers` propagate `null` instead of collapsing it via `safe(..., [])`. Then: (a) in `maySignalGroup`, `null` must return `{kind:"refuse", reason: "could not enumerate process group N — verification is impossible, so this group will NOT be signalled and the ownership record will NOT be deleted"}`, never `gone`; (b) in `ownsLiveRuntime`'s `stale` case, `null` must return `{live:true, detail: ...}`; (c) rewrite `ownership.test.ts:263` to assert the refusal, and add a teardown test that an unenumerable group yields `ok:false` and leaves `.sentinal/runtime.pid` on disk.

issues.title: preflight deletes the ownership record for a possibly-live orphan group whenever the contract declares no `http` readiness probe
issues.description:
In `src/runtime/preflight.ts`, `bound()` (:199-200) short-circuits to `false` when `readinessEndpoint(config)` is null — i.e. for every `exec`-type readiness probe, and for any http target whose port cannot be derived. The `stale` branch (:263-273) is gated solely on `!(await bound())`, so for an `exec`-probe contract with a dead leader it ALWAYS takes the "port is free" path: it calls `removePidfile(projectPath, verdict.entry.pid)` and returns `kind:"spawn"`. If the recorded pgid still has live members (the routine `npm run dev` shell-wrapper-without-exec shape the branch's own comment at :260-262 describes), Sentinal has just discarded the only record of that group and spawned a second stack on top of it — a permanent orphan, and the record needed to reap it is gone.

The port probe is a proxy for liveness that simply does not exist for non-http contracts; the group-member probe does and is already written (`listGroupMembers`, and `ownsLiveRuntime`'s `stale` branch asks exactly this question).
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/runtime/preflight.ts`, before the `removePidfile` at :264, require BOTH that the port is unbound AND that the recorded group has no live members — e.g. `const orphanMembers = verdict.entry.pgid === null ? [] : listGroupMembers(verdict.entry.pgid, deps.probes ?? {}); if (!(await bound()) && orphanMembers.length === 0) { removePidfile(...); return spawn }` and fall through to the ownership-verified `stop(projectPath)` reap otherwise. Add a `lifecycle.test.ts` row for 'exec-probe contract, dead leader, live group member' asserting the record is NOT deleted and the group is reaped (or refused).

issues.title: `ps -o pid= -g <pgid>` is not portable process-group selection — the plan's own first-listed form was the portable one
issues.description:
`realListGroup` (src/runtime/ownership.ts:192) selects group members with `ps -o pid= -g <pgid>`. This flag is not portable:

- macOS/Darwin ps(1) documents `-g` as "Ignored; for compatibility with earlier versions of ps." If that applies on any supported Darwin release, the command degrades to a bare `ps -o pid=` (controlling-terminal processes of the current user), which would enumerate an unrelated set or nothing at all — and combined with the must_fix above, 'nothing' currently reads as 'the group is gone'.
- On Linux/procps, `-g grplist` selects by **session id**, not process group id. Because `spawnDetached` uses `setsid()` (sid === pgid === pid for the leader), this returns a superset of the real group. That superset is benign here — every member of a session we created is our descendant — but it means the verification witness may come from a different process group than the one about to be signalled.

The only thing currently standing between the Darwin case and a silent empty enumeration is one real-process test (`ownership.test.ts:207-222`, "finds a REAL detached child by its process group"), which passes on the implementer's macOS box. The plan itself listed the portable form FIRST (`ps -o pid=,pgid=,command= -A`) and the `-g` form as the alternative.
issues.suggested_fix: Switch `realListGroup` in `src/runtime/ownership.ts:190-205` to the portable enumeration the plan named first: `ps -A -o pid=,pgid=`, parse both columns, and filter `row.pgid === pgid`. This is exact on both Darwin and Linux and removes the session-vs-group ambiguity. Keep `ownership.test.ts:207` (the real-child test) as the regression canary, and add an assertion that a sibling process in a DIFFERENT group within the same session is excluded.

issues.title: Guard 5 fails OPEN by default — the same defect class as the guard-3 gap this task just fixed
issues.description:
`forceCleanupOrphans` (src/worktree/cleanup.ts:128-129) resolves guard 5 as `opts.ownsLiveRuntime ?? config.ownsLiveRuntime ?? (() => ({ live: false }))`. When neither is supplied the guard is silently disabled and `--force` deletes directories with no liveness check — structurally identical to the pre-existing guard-3 defect the plan documents at line 196 ("Guard 3 is therefore dead in production today"). The path is reachable: `registerWorktreeTools` (src/worktree/mcp-tools.ts) falls back to `DEFAULT_WORKTREE_CONFIG` on its backwards-compatibility branch (bare `MemoryStore`/`null` deps), which carries no `ownsLiveRuntime`, and `cleanup-mcp-tool.ts`'s direct path passes no `ownsLiveRuntime` in `opts` — it relies entirely on the config having been threaded from `src/mcp/server.ts`. Only a static call-site test (`src/runtime/worktree-deps.test.ts`) protects this, and a future construction site added elsewhere would inherit the fail-open default with nothing going red.

The backward-compatibility argument for the permissive default is weaker than it looks: the default only applies to `force: true`, which is already opt-in and DESTRUCTIVE.
issues.suggested_fix: In `src/worktree/cleanup.ts:128-129`, make the absent-resolver default conservative for the `force` pass: `const ownsLiveRuntime = opts.ownsLiveRuntime ?? config.ownsLiveRuntime;` and if it is `undefined`, either (a) skip the entire `force` pass and push a warning ("force cleanup was requested but no liveness resolver was supplied — refusing to delete directories without a running-process check"), or (b) default to `() => ({ live: true, detail: "no liveness resolver was injected" })`. Add a `cleanup.test.ts` case asserting that an un-injected manager does not remove an orphan under `force: true`.

issues.title: The new `RUNTIME_STOP_FAILED` abort on `abandon` has no confirmed actionable surface through the sidecar route
issues.description:
`WorktreeManager.stopOwnedRuntime` (src/worktree/manager.ts:167-181) now throws `WorktreeError(..., "RUNTIME_STOP_FAILED")`, and `abandon`/`squashMerge` propagate it. On the MCP direct path the tool's `catch (err) { mcpError(...) }` surfaces the message. On the sidecar path, `handleAbandonWorktree` (src/sidecar/worktree-routes.ts:87-97) `await`s `manager.abandon(worktree_id)` with no local try/catch and returns `ok(...)` unconditionally; whether the caller sees the actionable remedy text ("delete .sentinal/runtime.pid yourself", the pids in the way, the `ps -o pid=,pgid=,command= -g N` command) depends entirely on a generic wrapper in the router. Since the sidecar path is the DEFAULT path for `worktree_abandon` (`mcp-tools.ts` prefers `client.abandonWorktree`), losing the reason there turns a designed refusal into an opaque 500 — and an agent that cannot see why abandon failed is an agent that reaches for `rm -rf`, which is the incident class this phase exists to prevent.

Related: with the abort in place, a worktree whose stop keeps refusing cannot be abandoned, cannot be merged, and is skipped by `worktree_cleanup --force` (guard 5). The only recovery is manually deleting `.sentinal/runtime.pid`. That IS named inside `outcome.reason` for the unreadable/foreign/refuse cases and is a legitimate escape hatch, but it is not documented anywhere a user will look first.
issues.suggested_fix: Wrap the `await manager.abandon(...)` in `src/sidecar/worktree-routes.ts:94` in `try/catch` and return `fail(err.message, 409)` for a `WorktreeError` with `code === "RUNTIME_STOP_FAILED"` so the full remedy text reaches the caller verbatim; add a `worktree-routes.test.ts` case asserting the response body contains the pid/pgid and the pidfile path. Separately, document the manual escape hatch (delete `<worktree>/.sentinal/runtime.pid` after confirming by hand what is running) in the README section Task 7 added, next to the `runtime_stop` docs.

issues.title: The `pgid === pid` fallback in `spawnDetached` is safe but untested for the reaped-leader case it exists for
issues.description: `spawnDetached` (src/runtime/spawn.ts) records `pgid: resolvePgid(pid) ?? (process.platform === "win32" ? null : pid)`. The reasoning is sound and I could not find a path where this over-optimistic pgid enables an unsafe signal: a reaped leader makes `inspectPidfile` return `stale`, so `leaderVerified` is false in `maySignalGroup` and the member-enumeration gate applies — the fabricated pgid can only ever produce a refusal or a no-op, never a kill of a stranger. But the fallback branch is only reachable in a race (leader exits before `ps` answers) and there appears to be no test that forces it, so a future edit that also relaxed the gate (e.g. treating a recorded pgid as provenance) would not be caught.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a test in `src/runtime/spawn.test.ts` that injects a `resolvePgid` returning `null` (or spawns `sh -c 'exit 0'` and retries until the fallback fires) and asserts the recorded pgid equals the pid; pair it with a `teardown.test.ts` case proving that a fabricated pgid whose live members do not reference the worktree still produces `ok:false`.

issues.title: The three unplanned modules are justified and correctly placed, but their inertness is load-bearing and only statically asserted
issues.description:
Each unplanned module is justified: `ownership.ts` (Task 2's documented note — `processBelongsToSandbox` does not generalise, and one shared refuse-to-signal gate beats three copies), `preflight.ts` (a decision function that also spawns cannot be tested exhaustively; the split kept `lifecycle.ts` under 400), and `worktree-deps.ts` (one production supplier for three resolvers instead of five inline copies, which is a sharper guard against Pre-Mortem #3). `worktree-deps.ts` respects the no-module-cycle rule in the correct direction — it lives in `src/runtime/` and imports `DEFAULT_WORKTREE_CONFIG`/`WorktreeConfig` from `src/worktree/types.js`, never the reverse — and `src/worktree/cleanup.ts` takes `RuntimeLiveVerdict` from `./types.js` rather than from the runtime domain.

The residual concern is that all three injected deps are optional and default to inert no-ops, so any construction site that forgets them silently disables `abandon`'s stop-on-exit, guard 5, and the R11 warning — with a static call-site test as the only guard.
issues.suggested_fix: Make `src/runtime/worktree-deps.test.ts` enumerate `new WorktreeManager(` call sites from source and assert the set is EXHAUSTIVE (fail on any new site outside `src/worktree/` that does not pass `runtimeWorktreeConfig`), rather than asserting only the five known sites.

truths.truth: runtime_up in worktree A writes <A>/.sentinal/runtime.pid containing a pid and (POSIX) a pgid, invisible to git status
truths.evidence: `writePidfile` (src/runtime/pidfile.ts:116-136) writes the zod-validated `{pid,pgid,startedAt,command,state}` shape then calls `excludeFromGit(worktreePath, [RUNTIME_PIDFILE_RELATIVE_PATH, RUNTIME_LOG_RELATIVE_PATH])` and surfaces (does not swallow) tier-3 warnings; `spawnDetached` returns the pid and its docblock mandates writing with `state="starting"` before the first poll. Covered by `src/runtime/pidfile.test.ts` (319 lines).

truths.truth: runtime_stop in A terminates A's process group; a process started from worktree B survives
truths.evidence: `stopOwnedGroup` signals only `-entry.pgid` (teardown.ts:293-323) after `maySignalGroup` clears it; there is no PID-pattern matching anywhere in the module. Task 3 DoD asserts `stopOwnedGroup` kills the group while a process outside it survives (`teardown.test.ts`, 515 lines).

truths.truth: runtime_up on an occupied port with no pidfile fails, and no alternative port is attempted anywhere in the code path
truths.evidence: `preflight` `case "absent"` (preflight.ts:309-321) returns `kind:"fail"` with `OCCUPIED_PORT_RULE` appended. `readinessEndpoint`/`readinessPort` derive the port solely from the project's declared probe; the file contains no arithmetic on a port, no free-port search and no retry loop. `isPortBound` connects-first then bind-probes (:157-163) — the macOS SO_REUSEADDR fix is correct and makes the probe strictly more likely to report 'bound', i.e. it errs toward hard-failing rather than proceeding.

truths.truth: A leader exiting non-zero before readiness fails fast; a leader exiting zero (detaching starter) continues polling
truths.evidence: Task 3 DoD is checked and `src/runtime/readiness.ts` (205 lines) + `readiness.test.ts` (187 lines) exist, but I did not read `readiness.ts` within the review budget and so cannot independently confirm that the zero-exit branch keeps polling rather than doing only a final probe.

truths.truth: abandon and squashMerge on a worktree with a live owned group stop it before removing the directory
truths.evidence: `squashMerge` awaits `this.stopOwnedRuntime(wt)` at manager.ts:214 — before `git checkout base` (:217), as the plan's risk row required, not merely before `worktree remove` (:229). `abandon` awaits it at :246, before the `existsSync` block AND before the `rmSync` fallback (:257) that git cannot veto. The no-pidfile fast path is real (teardown.ts:167-176 returns before `loadRuntimeConfig` is even called) and is proved by sentinel-absence, not a stopwatch, in `src/runtime/worktree-deps.test.ts:103-123` (stopOwnedGroup) and :172-187 (abandon end-to-end through a real manager with `down: touch <sentinel>`).

truths.truth: runtime_stop refuses to signal a PID whose cmdline does not reference the worktree
truths.evidence: `inspectPidfile` returns `foreign` for an alive pid failing `processBelongsToWorktree` (pidfile.ts:278-288) and `stopOwnedGroup` refuses `unreadable`/`foreign` before reaching any signal (teardown.ts:178-189). `processBelongsToWorktree` conflates 'someone else's' with 'could not tell' by design (ownership.ts:164-186); the symlink fix compares cwd against the literal AND `realpathSync` form of the SAME directory, which widens nothing. The orphan-reap row is genuinely implemented: `maySignalGroup` bypasses enumeration only when `leaderVerified && pgid === leaderPid`, and a dead leader forces `verifiedGroupMembers` to produce at least one witness or `refuse` (ownership.ts:291-318), asserted by `ownership.test.ts:307-379` (including 'verified leader whose pgid is NOT its own pid still enumerates'). Caveat: see the must_fix — the refusal is bypassed when enumeration FAILS rather than returns members.

truths.truth: A seeded worktree whose runtime.json declares "database": "shared" produces a notIsolatedWarning naming database
truths.evidence: Task 6 DoD is checked with named behavioural tests (`worktree-routes.test.ts` 'names the runtime contract's shared resources', `cli/commands/worktree.test.ts` real-binary spawn, `runtime/worktree-deps.test.ts`), and `runtimeWorktreeConfig` supplies `sharedResourcesFor` (worktree-deps.ts:51-52). I did not read `create.test.ts`/`reconcile.ts` to confirm all three seed sites thread their own path variable, so this is uncertain rather than verified.

truths.truth: src/worktree/manager.ts is under 400 lines, and src/worktree/** still imports nothing from src/runtime/**
truths.evidence: `manager.ts` is 298 lines (read to EOF). The runtime deps travel as data on `WorktreeConfig`: `cleanup.ts` imports `RuntimeLiveVerdict` from `./types.js`, `mcp-tools.ts` takes `worktreeConfig` threaded down from `src/mcp/server.ts`, and the only bridge module `src/runtime/worktree-deps.ts` sits on the runtime side importing from `../worktree/types.js` — correct direction. `src/sidecar/client.ts` does not appear in the Phase 4 diff at all (untouched, still 582).
